it is reasonable to say and correct to admit that like the rest of the nation and indeed the world, loudoun county is in the midst of a mental health and behavioral health substance use crisis. The nation is experiencing political division and financial uncertainty. However, it is also correct to note that loudoun county continues to whether the many storms of the past few years

more successfully than almost any other county in the nation. Loudoun, tonight we will discuss some of the challenges we face, some of the successes we have had in addressing those challenges and some of the strengths we share as a community that will enable us to achieve our goals going forward. In 2010 our nation began to see a marked increase

in anxiety disorders, depression, and even suicidology, especially among our youth. Unfortunately, loudoun was not immune to that phenomenon. In the book the ancient generation social psychologist jonathan put forward hypothesis for the mental health crisis faced by our young people today. Chief among the causes, he postulates the use of smart phones among

our youth have impacted everything from their ability to sleep, to their anxiety levels, social competitiveness, agitation, and perfectionism. To quote, there was a sudden and very large upturn in major depressive disorders beginning around 2012. He went on to say the percentage of U.S. Teens who have had at least one major depressive disorder episode increased by approximately 150%

since 2010. This increased happened across all races and social classes. In short, the extensive use of social media is having a deleterious effect -- impact on our nation' s youth. For our girls, excessive social media use and promote unrealistic goals for appearance causing them to have a negative opinion of themselves and unattainable

beauty standards. For boys, social media and especially gaming, especially gaming, can increase agitation, hostility, social anxiety, and disconnectedness. Loudoun, that is the bad news. That is the challenge. However, there is some good news or at least there is a reasonable response to this crisis. Just as it is true for physical health conditions, the answers to mental and behavioral health conditions are not monolithic.

For some, the answers are long-term and multilayered. For others, especially our youth, a good part of the answer can be routine behavior changes such as for a time putting away their electronic devices, going outside, getting exercise, fresh air, son, social

interaction. Although that might sound all too simplistic, the connection between mental health and physical connectivity is well documented. While no level of government to include the local level can or should try to address every issue or impact the rules and practices regarding social media in individuals homes, we certainly have the ability to address some of the negative impacts of an extensive social media use that can harm all of us but most especially our preteens

and teens just as they are developing their sense of self. Obviously, loudoun' s department of mental health substance abuse and developmental services grapples with the increase mental health conditions resulting from extensive social media use. However, they' re not the only county professionals committed to addressing this issue. A report from the mental health foundation released in MAY of '

24 details the importance of movement and exercise on mental health. According to the report the benefits of movement for mental health are improved mood, reduced anxiety, lowered inflammation and stress, improved memory it -- and concentration, increase confidence, improved sleep, and increased social connectedness. Thus, it has become clear that although loudoun' s department of parks and rec and community

services is not involved in treating the mental health issues, ensuring our young people have ample opportunities to engage in physical activity and competition should be included in an overall wellness program. Thus, the staff at the parks and rec department can have an essential role promoting comprehensive mental health wellness. In loudoun,

our parks and rec department led by the ever present steve tour b continues to advocate for more opportunities to increase our greed and open spaces. Parks and rec works to ensure our citizens and visitors enjoy her marvelous county and have unique outdoor experiences. The dedicated members of our parks and rec staff are also committed to investing in our future generations by giving them opportunities to have their voices heard. One such

initiative created by parks and rec is the pathway to pages program. Parks and rec invited county students from kindergarten through fifth grade who -- to participate in the county after school activities to create a nature-based story for the pathways to pages contest. The students were required to write original stories and create their own illustrations. The two winning entries were rabbit

hole from the hutchison farm elementary school C.A.S.A. Program and loudoun county parks who attends the madison trust elementary school program. Rabbit hole is a wonderful story of animals helping animals and includes many of the animals found in our parks. Loudoun county parks is an explanation of awareness and highlights the amenities

offered within our park. By finding creative ways to involve and engage elementary aged kids to connect with our parks and open spaces or to just go outside and be kids, young aylwin and brady MAY not know it but in their own way, they are on the frontlines of battling the nation' s mental health crisis. Loudoun, so much of what we do in county government is to prepare a path for generations to follow. Tonight it is my distinct pleasure to introduce you to

two reasons why I feel our future is in very good hands. Aylwin and brandon are here tonight with their parents and families. Please welcome them along with parks and rec director steve and his staff.

[Applause] congratulations. The challenge of mental health and substance use has been what our entire nation is confronting. Unfortunately, all too often, law enforcement is the first call when a person is having a mental health or substance use crisis and while law enforcement officers are highly trained professionals, most do not have extensive training in mental health or crisis

intervention. Having a clear understanding of mental illness the most law enforcement professional loudoun county sheriff mike chapman set a goal to have 100% of his forced equipped with crisis intervention training or cit. with the exception of new deputies, close to 100% of all sheriff deputies in loudoun county are cit trained. The goal with cit is to train law enforcement officers to recognize people suffering from

a mental health crisis. De-escalating the situation reduces injury to the officer and citizen. Identifying the appropriate resource to provided the needing services and care to a citizen reduces recidivism and prevents firmer traumatizing a person who MAY be having one of the worst moments of their life. In addition to having his officers trained in cit, sheriff chapman has been a champion of funding and opening a crisis intervention center in loudoun. Currently, when someone is experiencing a mental health

crisis, a law enforcement officer is required to stay with them in the hospital or urgent care setting. Remaining in a nonclinical setting for hours often further destabilizes a person experiencing a mental health crisis. In addition, it takes law enforcement officers off of the street leading to a reduction in personnel available to respond to calls. Those of us who have experienced a physical health

emergency understand how hard it would be to sit in pain in an emergency room for an untold amount of time. It is no easier for a person experiencing a mental health emergency. After all, mental health is health. A cic will provide mental and behavioral health short-term care for people who are experiencing a mental health

emergency. A cic facility will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week employing a team of multidisciplinary professionals. The cic officers destabilization will determine if they require further treatment or they can safely return home. Loudoun, sheriff mike chapman and fire chief keith johnson both understand the importance of immediate and proper care for those suffering a mental or behavioral health crisis. This immediate and

proper care extends to our first responders as well. Although we all understand being a law enforcement officer is a dangerous profession, we are never really prepared when one of her own sheriff' s deputies finds themselves in the line of duty life-threatening moment. On JANUARY 2nd, 2021, deputy sustained a life-threatening injury as a result of a

seemingly routine call. What I and so many others now realize and what our first responders have always known is this, there is no such thing as a routine call for them. Because every call could be there last. That daily knowledge combined with the stress of choosing a profession with round-the-clock work hours, ongoing exposure to traumatic events, and sleep deprivation has resulted in our first responders having higher

than average divorce and depression rates and ptsd that is four times higher than the population. The rates of domestic violence incidents and suicidal ideation are also higher than the general public. Perhaps the most alarming statistic is this, the number of death by suicides of our nations law enforcement is higher than the number of line of duty deaths. Realizing that our first responders mental

wellness has to be a top priority. In fiscal year 2018, chief johnson of our combined fire and rescue system requested the county board approve a behavioral health coordinator assigned specifically and exclusively to work with fire and rescue professionals and volunteer staff and now, in fiscal year ' 25 at the request of sheriff chapman, we' ve approved the position with similar responsibilities for sheriff' s

office. [Applause] if you question whether these positions are necessary, you need only ask cameron, the loudoun county deputy who was severely wounded when answering that seemingly routine to call in 2021. He applied a tourniquet that likely saved the deputy'

s life. While deputy gentry has dealt with physical wounds, both of these deputies continue to deal with and address the long-term mental health ramifications of that experience and both have shown incredible courage because they discuss the importance of addressing the nonphysical drama of the incident publicly addressing the mental health scars they' ve obtained, deputy gentry and ewing will reduce the stigma on this issue and encourage other

first responders to seek mental and behavioral health support when needed. Loudoun, please join me in honoring all of our first responders I welcoming sheriff mike chapman chief williams and all of the first responders in the room, can you please stand so that we can show you our appreciation.
